title: The youngest son
hookLine: passing over his elder sons, Guru Ram Das names his youngest, Arjan, as the fifth Guru

lines: THE YOUNGEST, STILL A YOUNG MAN.
cards: At a family dinner there's the one who talks first, and the one who mostly listens. Guru Ram Das and Bibi Bhani had three sons.
The eldest, Prithi Chand, was capable and ambitious, and managed much of the growing community's practical business. Tradition says he fully expected to be the next Guru.
The middle son, Mahadev, was gentle and withdrawn, and seemed to want nothing to do with worldly affairs. And the youngest was Arjan: quiet, devoted, still a young man.

teach.h: ARJAN, CHOSEN AS THE FIFTH GURU.
teach.b: Guru Ram Das chose Arjan. Tradition dates it to 1581, when Arjan was about eighteen. It made Prithi Chand bitterly angry; more on that in a couple of days.
Why Arjan? Sikh tradition tells of a test.

teach.h: SENT TO LAHORE, TOLD TO WAIT.
teach.b: The Guru needed someone to go to Lahore, to represent the family at a relative's wedding, and to stay there until he was called back.

Prithi Chand found a reason not to go; he didn't want to be far away while the succession was being decided. Mahadev wasn't interested. Arjan simply went, and waited, far from home, for a very long time.

What happened while he waited is tomorrow's story. For today, look at the pattern; it has come up on this path before. Guru Nanak passed over his own sons for Lehna, the man who carried the wet grass.
Guru Angad chose the old water carrier. Guru Amar Das chose the orphan with the tray of grams. Now Guru Ram Das passes over the confident eldest son for the quiet youngest.

teach.h: NOT THE ONE WHO PUSHED FORWARD.
teach.b: Each time, the one who was ready wasn't the one who pushed forward. It was the one who served, and waited, and didn't make the moment about himself.
One thing changes here: from now on, the Guruship stays in Guru Ram Das's family.

teach.h: NOT THE LOUDEST: THE READY ONE.
teach.b: The rule doesn't: not the eldest, not the loudest, but the one who is ready.
And with that choice, Guru Ram Das's part of the story closes: the orphan, the pool, the four rounds, the youngest son.

how: Sikhs honor Guru Arjan as the fifth Guru, chosen by his father, Guru Ram Das; the story of his choosing is told as another sign that the Guruship went to the one most devoted, not the one first in line.

o: Guru Ram Das's brother and advisor
the youngest son, chosen as fifth Guru
the middle son, who shunned the world

games.q: who's who among the brothers — tap the pairs.
p: the eldest, who expected to lead
where Arjan was sent to wait

s: the fifth Guru was the eldest son
Guru Ram Das chose his youngest son, Arjan.
Arjan went to Lahore when his father asked
Prithi Chand found a reason not to go; Arjan went and waited.
every Guru so far had chosen the most senior candidate
again and again, they chose the one who served and waited.

games.q: you're Guru Ram Das, choosing a successor. your eldest son is capable and expects it. your youngest is quiet and went where you sent him. whom do you choose?
o: no one yet; wait and see.
games.why: Guru Ram Das named Arjan, his youngest, as the fifth Guru. the quiet one was ready.

practice: Bring to mind someone quietly ready, in your family, your office, your team or your friends: the one who doesn't talk much in meetings but always gets it done, or who's been waiting patiently for a chance nobody's given them.
Hold their face in mind, and think what they'd do if someone trusted them with more.

wordCard.voice: Arjan. The youngest of Guru Ram Das's three sons, chosen over his elder brothers to become the fifth Guru.
